trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Cell (3,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,1).
I can't rule out to (4,2) or to (6,1) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (4,2).
Going to (4,3) would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (6,2).
Cell (6,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,1).
Going to (7,3) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (8,2).
Cell (9,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (9,3).
Going to (8,3) would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (9,5).
The line must go to (9,6): to (8,5) is number 6, which comes later.
Going to (8,6) would strand number 4: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (9,7).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (8,7).
Going to (6,6) would cut off the bottom edge (6 cells). So the line goes to (7,5).

Going to (6,5) would leave both cell (6,3) and cell (6,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going to (7,3) would leave both cell (6,3) and cell (8,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (8,5).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (8,3).
Going to (1,5), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 9. So the line goes to (2,6).
Number 9 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (1,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (1,3).
Going to (2,3) would strand number 10: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (1,2).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,2).
Cell (4,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,5).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
